newsitem.title: USA: Money managers remained short on U.S. debt-survey.
newsitem.headline: Money managers remained short on U.S. debt-survey.

text.p: U.S. money managers continued to take short positions in U.S. debt markets over the past week, said a survey by Stone & McCarthy Research Associates Inc.
"Particpants ... remain short and getting shorter, although the rate has slowed this week," the report said.
"Money managers actively adjusted portfolio structure again over the past week, reducing duration exposure and raising cash further in the process," it said.
In the week ended January 21, duration bogey slipped to 4.17 from 4.20 an arithmetic basis and dropped to 4.76 from 4.89 on a weighted basis.

Duration refers to a portfolio's average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk. Duration bogey is the level of asset or liability duration sought in the management of a portfolio.

The survey's bear/bull index fell to 4.66 from 5.12 the prior week on an arithmetic basis. It fell to 4.07 from 5.15 on an asset-weighted basis. A number above 5.00 is seen as indicating investors are mostly long on the market.
The cash/assets ratio rose to 7.52 percent from 7.16 percent.
Eight percent of the portfolio managers polled said they were planning to be active in the coming week, down from 12 percent the week before.
The bear/bull index collected among those intending to be active rose to 5.00 from 4.67 the previous week.
The Stone & McCarthy survey is conducted by the research firm weekly. It includes 25 market participants with total assets of about $100 billion, the firm said.
* Table provided by Stone and McCarthy Research Associates.
** Respondents intending to adjust portfolio in coming week.
